title: It's All in the Preparation
description: The three columns of pronouns and the prepositions that hold a testimony together: subject pronouns (I, we, you, he, she, it, they), object pronouns (me, us, you, him, her, it, them) and possessive adjectives (my, our, your, his, her, its, their), where each column stands in the sentence (subject before the verb, object after the verb or after any preposition, possessive immediately before a noun) and how to say what a pronoun points back at inside a text; the prepositions of place, time, direction and company (at, in, on, to, from, for, with, about) and the verbs that keep their own preposition (work in, get on well with, think of or about, listen to, depend on); the reading skills of the lesson - filling an information file from a spoken testimony (name, age, occupation, family size, father's job, mother's job) and explaining a sentence in your own words, that is choosing another form to express the same content about yourself or about somebody else; and the vocabulary of the lesson (freedom, a chef, a nurse, cookery, a mobile, a wedding, a struggle, a loan, to get on well with somebody)
